implementation_notes: No language provides the abstraction — that is the point of the pattern catalog, and the choice of merge point is the actual work. The detection is a clone detector over the whole tree including tests and configuration, ranked by size and by how often the clones change together; type-3 near-miss clones with nontrivial differences matter more than exact copies because they are where the design knowledge lives. The ladder is Fowler's: Extract Method when the expression repeats within a class, Extract Method then Pull Up Method for sibling subclasses, Substitute Algorithm when the copies do the same thing by different means, and Extract Component (Extract Class) when the copies are in unrelated classes. Above that, the shape of the copies selects the pattern: a parameter list that repeats is a parameter object, a growing family of parallel conditionals is a strategy, and a concern needed at every call site is a decorator or interceptor rather than a merge target. Apply the rule of three as a trigger for whether the merge pays for itself.
idiom_name: Extract Method / Extract Component; then the right pattern for the shape
pitfalls: Fixing the bug in one copy only — the highest-severity instance of the smell.
Over-abstracting: a shared function with four flags is worse than the copies and harder to remove.
A cross-cutting copy cannot be merged into one place; it needs a decorator or interceptor instead.
Trusting a detector's output as a plan: near-miss clones may differ intentionally, which is why merge tools ask a human to choose the abstraction.
